A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSPC diffusion-generalization work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and added content.

before.justification: v2 reports original denoiser-error and gradient analyses, PSPC-generated samples, and CIFAR-10 SSCD comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds CFDM comparisons and further architecture-dependent analyses in Appendix D.

M1.justification: PSPC aggregation, square-patch scheduling, gradient-based flexible patches, and nearest-neighbour posterior estimation remain unchanged. The new boundary-handling explanation documents the existing cropping definition.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, FFHQ at 64×64, and AFHQv2 at 64×64 through denoising and diffusion sampling. Additional network configurations introduce no new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: CFDM moves from citation-only coverage in v2 to evaluated comparisons in v3 Figures 7 and 9. Figure 9 also adds PSPC-Square, while Appendix D adds neural-to-neural MSE comparisons and additional reference networks, substantially broadening direct comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes the reported gradient-analysis sample count from 10,000 to 1,000; whether experiments were rerun is unspecified. v3 also introduces 50k FID reporting and patch-error evaluations using additional networks' reverse processes. Existing training settings and the SSCD protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests whether gradient locality and patch-size behaviour extend beyond DDPM++, adding NCSN++ and DiT gradient analyses and additional transformer patch-error analyses. Figures 9 and 25 also extend the Square-versus-Flex comparison to generated samples, materially expanding validation of the proposed mechanism.

E5.justification: The reporting practice remains point estimates and averages, including SSCD averages over 1,000 shared initializations. No repeated-training results, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests are added. The gradient sample-count revision concerns evaluation sample size.

E6.justification: v3 adds CFDM error curves, extensive cross-network results, FID scores in Table 3, and new sampling comparisons. Figure 9 adds CFDM's mean network similarity of 0.23 and PSPC-Square entries, while retaining the original submatrix and PSPC-Flex mean of 0.55.

T1.justification: Equation (8) corrects the denoiser argument from x to noisy input z in the formal gradient-sensitivity definition, resolving its inconsistency with differentiation with respect to z. The posterior definitions, PSPC equations, and mathematical reasoning otherwise remain unchanged; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: shared local inductive biases, patch denoising as a partial generalization mechanism, and PSPC's similarity to network outputs. Additional evidence supports these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 explicitly discusses PSPC's remaining approximation gap relative to other neural denoisers and identifies closing it as future work. Section 7 newly explains why localized patch sets can benefit spatially aligned FFHQ images. The existing sampling-artifact limitation remains.

D1.justification: The introduction adds access information for an open-source implementation of PSPC and other denoisers. Section 4 explicitly clarifies that square cropping excludes patches requiring boundary padding. Existing architecture tables, training hyperparameters, and patch schedules are retained.

R1.justification: Section 7 substantially expands positioning within classical patch synthesis and single-image GAN/diffusion research, adding works such as PatchMatch, SinGAN, SinFusion, and SinDiffusion. It also develops the comparison with Kamb and Ganguli around localized patch sets and architectural scope.

P1.justification: v3 edits grammar and expands explanations of locality, gradient indexing, and patch posterior means. It inserts Appendix D, renumbers the retained qualitative appendices, and adds acknowledgements and publication information. The main section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds a FID table and several analytical figures, expands Figure 9 from a 7×7 to a 9×9 matrix, and adds Figure 25. Retained denoiser grids are arranged two per page, and v2 Figures 21–23 are consolidated into v3 Figure 24 without changing their samples.

improvement.justification: Appendix D addresses an important evidential weakness: v2's locality and patch-error analyses focused on DDPM++, despite the central claim spanning architectures. Direct checks on additional CNN and transformer denoisers substantially strengthen that claim. CFDM and neural-peer comparisons better establish PSPC's strengths and remaining gap. Some new baseline documentation remains incomplete, but the improved empirical support and added code-access information provide a substantial overall gain.
